title: Rough Plumbing Coordination: Wet Vent Constraints, Vent Routing, and Exterior Drain Tie-In (This Old House)

locations.name: Basement

summary: This Old House guides a rough plumbing layout in a partially finished home, focusing on venting when LVLs block a conventional wet-vent arrangement, and then detailing how a 3-inch drain from the primary bathroom is routed through the garage and foundation to an exterior sewer tie-in. The crew reroutes vents through floor joists to avoid attic space and moves vent termination to the opposite side of the roof, while concealing new drain lines behind a partition wall in the finished basement. The video covers practical decisions about where to vent, how to run drains with pitch, and how to integrate an exterior sewer connection while the interior remains finished.

sections.title: Vent strategy when LVLs block wet vent
sections.description: The team explains why a standard wet vent can’t be used due to LVL blocking, necessitating individual drain venting for the toilet and shower instead of tying them into a single wet-vent run.

sections.title: Routing vents to the side of the roof and attic avoidance
sections.description: To keep attic space clear, vents are run through existing floor joists and connected to a roof vent on the opposite side rather than a straight-through roof line.

sections.title: Independent drain and vent paths for fixtures
concepts: avoidance of wet vent due to LVL
sections.description: With structural constraints, separate drain and vent paths are created for the tub and toilet instead of relying on a single wet vent arrangement.

sections.title: 3-inch drain routing from primary bathroom toward garage
sections.description: A 3-inch drain is run from the upstairs primary bathroom toward the garage area, maintaining proper pitch toward the final fixture.

sections.title: Concealing drainage in a finished basement
sections.description: Because the basement is finished, drain pipes are hidden behind a 2x6 partition wall while routing along the foundation wall.

sections.title: Exterior exit and sewer main tie-in planning
sections.description: The plan calls for exiting the drain outside the building and tying into the sewer main, coordinating with exterior drainage routing.

sections.title: Next steps: finish rough and stop water piping
sections.description: The presenter asks about completing the rough drain work on the remaining side and finishing water piping as the next steps.
